text.tspan: Everyday English - B2 - 2026/06/08 - 01 - Essay
Hands cultivate a garden with care.
Pexels · 7729129
Growing something small
A good way to care for a plant combines practical structure with an awareness of other people. Neither a rigid plan nor complete
improvisation is sufficient on its own; both need to be judged in context.
The practical case is straightforward: observing a plant helps us respond to what it needs. Consider how we check whether the soil
feels dry before adding water. The benefit is not merely efficiency. A modest arrangement prevents avoidable confusion, leaving
attention available for the activity itself rather than for problems that could have been anticipated.
Consideration adds a second, equally important dimension: keeping a simple record helps us learn from changes. In this situation, we
note which window gives the plant enough light without scorching its leaves. A decision can be convenient for one person while
creating difficulty for another, so its value depends partly on whose needs it recognises.
The most useful approach therefore brings structure and consideration together. Preparation establishes a workable starting point;
attention to other people keeps it responsive. Success should be assessed by how well the arrangement serves the experience,
rather than by how closely events follow the original plan.
BUILD YOUR OWN · State a focused main idea. Develop one supporting reason in each body paragraph, with a concrete example.
Conclude by connecting the two reasons without introducing a new argument. Use the structure as a model; write about an
experience of your own.
Explain your reasoning to a partner. What two reasons support the main idea? Explain one example. (Model: The two reasons are that
observing a plant helps us respond to what it needs and that keeping a simple record helps us learn from changes. One example is
that we check whether the soil feels dry before adding water.)
